test_title: RRB Technician Grade 1 20 Dec 2024 Shift 1 Official Paper
subject: general
question: When p-n junction diode is biased, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Depletion layer gets wider when it is reverse biased.
Depletion layer gets narrower only when diode is forward biased and remains constant when it is reverse biased.
Depletion layer gets narrower when it is reverse biased.
Depletion layer gets wider only when diode is forward biased and remains constant when it is reverse biased.

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**p-n Junction Diode**

**Definition:** A p-n junction diode is a semiconductor device formed by joining p-type and n-type semiconductors. The interface where these two types meet is known as the p-n junction. This junction has unique properties that make it essential for various electronic devices, especially for rectification (converting AC to DC).

**Working Principle:**

The p-n junction diode operates based on the movement of charge carriers, namely electrons and holes, across the junction. When the diode is unbiased (i.e., no external voltage is applied), a depletion region forms at the junction due to the diffusion of electrons from the n-region to the p-region and holes from the p-region to the n-region. This region acts as an insulator preventing current flow.

**Biasing of p-n Junction Diode:**

Biasing refers to the application of an external voltage to a p-n junction diode, which can be done in two ways: forward bias and reverse bias.

 
• **Forward Bias:** In forward bias, the p-type side (anode) is connected to the positive terminal of the power supply, and the n-type side (cathode) is connected to the negative terminal. This reduces the width of the depletion layer, allowing current to flow through the diode.
 
• **Reverse Bias:** In reverse bias, the p-type side is connected to the negative terminal, and the n-type side is connected to the positive terminal. This increases the width of the depletion layer, preventing current flow through the diode.

 

The correct option is: Depletion layer gets wider when it is reverse biased.

This option is correct because, in reverse bias, the external voltage increases the barrier potential across the p-n junction. This causes more electrons to be pulled away from the junction in the n-region and more holes to be pulled away in the p-region, thus widening the depletion layer. This increased depletion layer acts as a stronger barrier to the flow of charge carriers, preventing current from flowing through the diode (except for a very small leakage current)
